content:
For Iris-Lean, we want to have a core library which does not depend on mathlib+cslib, and also an extended library which does have these dependencies. It would be nice to have everything in one github repository, like: 

├── Iris-Lean/
│   ├── lakefile.toml
│   └── src/
│       └── ...
├── Iris-Lean-Ext/
│   ├── lakefile.toml
│   └── src/
│       └── ...
└── lean-toolchain

Is there a way to set such a project up so that Iris-Lean and Iris-Lean-Ext get indexed by Reservoir as two separate packages? I don't think this setup meets the inclusion criteria as it stands. Alternatively, is there a way to combine Iris-Lean and Iris-Lean-Ext with a single lakefile at the top-level, but still allow them to be independently imported and for Iris-Lean to not have a Mathlib dependency?

Unfortunately, this project setup is not currently supported. However, I am planning to add a manual package registration to Reservoir this quarter which will support this. Still, having both packages in the same repository does impose a cost on users, as they will have to clone the full repository (i.e., the source of both) when requiring just the basic package.
Thank you for the reply! It sounds like the best thing to do for the time being is to use a separate repo, but I'll keep an eye out for the changes to package registration.

@Mac Malone We also have a repo where we'd prefer not to put the lakefile at the top level: https://github.com/cryspen/rust-core-models

What's the status of manual registration? That would be great to have!

@Alexander Bentkamp Admins can now manually register packages to Reservoir. Unfortunately, I did not manage to squeeze in subdirectories as part of that change. However, it should not take much to add. Please open an issue on leanprover/reservoir with the repository information. I will try to register it when I can. Sadly, though, I am quite busy. Is this something you need soon?
Thanks, @Mac Malone! There is no rush.
Much appreciated! I've made an issue too (and no rush for us either)

Mac Malone said:

Still, having both packages in the same repository does impose a cost on users, as they will have to clone the full repository (i.e., the source of both) when requiring just the basic package.

This is the same as the cost they would pay if the two were combined into a single package in the first place, right?

Eric Wieser said:

This is the same as the cost they would pay if the two were combined into a single package in the first place, right?

Yes. However, the proposal was to make them separate packages (and repositories). This would make the most sense as one package has many fewer dependencies.

Maybe the underlying problem here is that Mathlib is an agressive dependency which registers hooks that do very heavily installation work when you run lake update, unlike most other required packages which don't come with any cost except source code until, and you only pay compilation costs for what you actually import
I guess the question is whether the replacement of lake exe cache by lake cache is going to make mathlib stop doing this, or is going to make every other package start doing it as well.

FYI: We've refactored our repo setup and created a dedicated repo with a toplevel lakefile. A CI job copies the Lean subdirectory in our main repo to that dedicated Lean repo on every commit: https://github.com/cryspen/hax/blob/main/.github/workflows/deploy_hax_lean.yml
This not only a workaround for the missing subdirectory feature. We also do this to stop lake from downloading our entire repo.

So we don't need the subdirectory feature any more. Still, it might get useful in the future.
